name: FL-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+20 partisan lean in a seat held by Democrats
Wasserman Schultz holds a roughly 50-to-1 fundraising advantage over Andersen
Polymarket prices a Democratic win near 95%, the main source of residual caution

model.rationale: A South Florida seat that leans 20 points Democratic, paired with a well-known incumbent who has raised about $3.3 million against a challenger reporting under $65,000, leaves Brent Andersen with no evident path; prediction markets agree the Democrat is a heavy favorite, and the only open question is the size of the margin.
model.watch: Any fresh polling showing a single-digit race, a major scandal, or unusually low Democratic turnout could pull the expected margin back toward the market's more cautious pricing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) is running.

overview:
This South Florida House seat leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 20 points. Debbie Wasserman Schultz, a long-serving incumbent and former national party chair, was renominated and enters the general election with roughly $3.3 million raised and $1.9 million on hand. Republican Brent Andersen has reported about $64,000 raised and $41,000 in the bank, while outside spending in the race has been modest. An independent candidate trails far behind in both visibility and money.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, where Polymarket prices a Democratic win near 95%. Some residual uncertainty reflects the absence of polling and the unusual mid-cycle circumstances surrounding the seat. Even so, every measurable indicator points to a comfortable double-digit Democratic victory in November.
